title: Idli
description: Soft, steamed fermented rice-and-lentil cakes — a light, easily digestible staple, traditionally the anchor of a South Indian meal or breakfast.
steps: Soak the rice separately from the urad dal and fenugreek seeds, both in enough water to cover, for 4-6 hours.
Drain and grind the urad dal and fenugreek together to a smooth, fluffy batter, adding water as needed. Grind the rice separately to a slightly coarser paste.
Combine both batters, add salt, and mix well. The consistency should be thick but pourable.
Cover and let the batter ferment in a warm place for 8-12 hours, or overnight, until it has visibly risen.
Grease the idli plates lightly with oil and pour the fermented batter into each mould, filling about three-quarters full.
Steam in an idli steamer or a pressure cooker (without the weight/whistle) for 12-15 minutes, until a toothpick inserted comes out clean.
Let the idlis rest for a couple of minutes before unmoulding. Serve hot with chutney and sambar.
